summary.one_liner: OpenFang is an open-source Agent Operating System written in Rust that ships as a single ~32MB binary and runs autonomous agents ("Hands") on schedules.
summary.what_it_does: OpenFang is a Rust-built agent runtime with a CLI, daemon, and web dashboard. Its core feature is "Hands": pre-built autonomous capability packages (Clip, Lead, Collector, Predictor, Researcher, Twitter, Browser) that run on schedules without a prompt, each bundling a HAND.toml manifest, a system prompt playbook, a SKILL.md reference, and guardrails such as approval gates. The README says the project includes 40 messaging channel adapters, connections to 27 LLM providers, 53 built-in tools with MCP and A2A support, and a SQLite-backed memory layer with vector embeddings. It describes a security model of 16 layers, including a WASM sandbox, a Merkle hash-chain audit trail, taint tracking, and an OFP mutual-authentication protocol for P2P networking. It also provides an OpenAI-compatible API with 140+ REST/WS/SSE endpoints, a WhatsApp Web gateway that connects via QR code, and a migration command for importing from OpenClaw. The README is the source for these claims; the benchmark tables are self-reported by the project.
use_cases: run scheduled research and competitor monitoring agents
generate and score sales leads on a daily schedule
turn YouTube videos into captioned vertical shorts
manage a Twitter/X account with approval-gated posts
connect AI agents to Telegram, Discord, Slack, and WhatsApp
serve an OpenAI-compatible API backed by multiple LLM providers
notable: Autonomous 'Hands' that run on schedules without prompting, with approval gates for sensitive actions
Single ~32MB compiled binary with no pip or Docker install step
16 listed security layers including WASM sandbox, Merkle audit trail, and SSRF protection
40 channel adapters and an OpenAI-compatible API
Migration command for moving agents from OpenClaw
caveats: The README states v0.5.10 is pre-1.0, with breaking changes possible between minor versions; it advises pinning to a commit for production.
The README says some Hands are more mature than others, with Browser and Researcher described as most battle-tested.
Benchmark comparisons are self-reported by the project and are not independently verified in the README.
keywords: run ai agents on a schedule
